name: Boat Maintenance Checklist
description: Routine boat upkeep covering the engine, hull, bilge, electrical and fuel systems, plus seasonal winterizing tasks.

items.text: Check engine oil and coolant levels
Confirm the bilge pump and float switch work
Inspect the propeller for dings or fishing line
Check fuel level and look for leaks or fumes
Test navigation lights and electronics
Change engine oil and filter per the service schedule
Replace the water pump impeller at the recommended interval
Change lower-unit gear oil and check for water intrusion
Inspect belts, hoses and clamps for wear
Service spark plugs and check the cooling system flow
Flush the engine with fresh water after saltwater use
Inspect the hull for cracks, blisters or damage
Clean the hull and check antifouling paint condition
Check sacrificial anodes and replace worn ones
items.note: Anodes protect metal parts from galvanic corrosion

items.text: Inspect through-hull fittings and seacocks
Check cleats, rails and deck hardware are secure
Wax gelcoat and protect fittings from corrosion
Clean the bilge and remove oily residue
Test the bilge pump and clear the strainer
Check for any unexplained water entering the boat
Inspect freshwater and waste system hoses
Confirm the drain plug seals correctly
Check battery charge and clean the terminals
Inspect wiring for chafing, corrosion or loose connections
Test all lights, gauges and electronics
Inspect the fuel system for leaks and replace the filter
Check fuel hoses, fittings and the tank vent
Add fuel stabilizer or manage fuel per the manual
Fog the engine to protect internal parts
Drain cooling and water systems to prevent freezing
Charge or remove the battery for storage
Clean, dry and cover the boat for the off-season
Inspect the trailer tires, bearings and lights if applicable

faq.q: How often should I service my boat engine?
faq.a: Follow the engine manufacturer's schedule, which is usually based on engine hours and time. Common items include oil and filter changes, lower-unit gear oil, impeller and spark plug replacement, with severe or saltwater use shortening the intervals.

faq.q: Why is the bilge so important?
faq.a: The bilge collects water that gets into the boat, so a working bilge pump and float switch help keep the vessel afloat. Keep the bilge clean and dry, check the pump regularly and look for any unexplained water that could signal a leak.

faq.q: How do I protect against corrosion?
faq.a: Rinse with fresh water after saltwater trips, check sacrificial anodes and replace them when worn, and keep electrical connections clean and protected. Inspect through-hulls, fittings and the hull for corrosion or galvanic damage regularly.

Winterizing typically means stabilizing or draining fuel, fogging the engine, draining and protecting cooling and water systems from freezing, charging or removing the battery, and covering the boat. Follow your manuals, as steps vary by engine and climate.

faq.q: Can I print this boat maintenance checklist?
faq.a: Yes. Print it or download the PDF so you can keep it aboard or in the shed and log the date and engine hours each time you complete maintenance.
